title: Advanced Digital Mapping to Foster Territorial Supply and Demand Network of Secondary Raw Materials Towards Industrial Symbiosis Scenarios
content:
Ecology, metabolism, and industrial symbiosis have driven scientific research and field experimentation since the early 1990s, aiming to reduce waste, increase the reuse of resources already withdrawn from natural ecosystems, and valorise secondary raw materials, while supporting decarbonisation in the construction sector. Despite numerous European and international directives promoting circular economy principles throughout the building life cycle, significant legislative, political, operational, and cultural barriers persist. In particular, the limited availability of information on the location, management, and valorisation of secondary raw materials constrains the effective implementation of circular practices at both the production and end-of-life stages.
This paper presents the results of the first experimental digital platform for the multifactorial mapping and localisation of secondary raw materials in Sardinia, Italy, where shortages of both primary resources and recycling and reuse facilities call for innovative industrial symbiosis approaches. The digital mapping covers the main waste categories associated with the construction sector, including concrete, wood, glass, plastics, metals, and ceramics. It provides the basis for identifying potential scenarios for reusing waste streams in parallel industrial processes, supported by AI-based tools, while a user-centred interface facilitates interactions between supply and demand.
Results show that the platform can facilitate exchanges between waste producers and potential users, supporting territorial networks and more environmentally conscious waste-management practices. Its main limitation is the need for further operational testing with end users, which constitutes the focus of ongoing research.
